_: The plague profile: what a sickness is, as keys, drawn for every plague at its birth by a hash of the seed and the plague's id (never from the history's rolls). A biological plague is a list of symptoms in the order they come, an onset, a course and whom it takes; a memetic one is a form, a list of effects in the order they come, and a carrier. The names pass reads the profile (a sufferer names the sickness by the symptom it noticed, a neighbour by the host); the flavour of a plague is the whole list read in order.

symptoms: one row per symptom: key; noun (the word a name uses for it); adj (the adjective a name uses when it is the mark); visible marks the ones seen on the body (an engineered plague hides them); end says which bank the last symptom is drawn from by lethality: deadly (over 0.6), wasting (under 0.3), or either; desc is what it looks like. onsets, courses, takes: one row each with a desc. forms: the shape a memetic plague takes, with noun; hosted marks the forms that want a host, which a conscious one is drawn from. effects: what believers do, with severity 1 to 3; the last effect's severity follows lethality. carriers: what carries it.
Every term here is a technical term: a phrase a reader who never saw this project understands or can search for, never a coinage.

symptoms.desc: a fever that comes and goes and comes back
a cough that never quite clears
bleeding from the eyes, the gums, the skin
the sight goes, and does not come back
the sick talk to people who are not there, and then to nobody
the flesh goes off the bone over a season
the flesh dies while the body lives
growths that open like flowers on the skin
the sick grow quiet, then still, then absent
the skin turns the colour of ash
the eyes run and will not stop
hard clear growths under the skin, like glass
the tongue goes black, then the lips

onsets.desc: days from the first sign to the bed
a season of small signs before anyone is sure

courses.desc: it is over in days, one way or the other
it runs for years in the body
it is passed down, and the children have it before they are born

takes.desc: it takes one caste, one kind of body among them, and leaves the rest
it takes one blood and its kin and nothing else; it was made to

forms.desc: a question that cannot be put down once it is heard
a set of rules that explains everything
a joke that is only funny the second time
a refusal to say a certain thing, then any thing
a number that has to be counted to
a song that will not leave the head
a dream everyone has the same night
an argument with no last word
a certainty, about nothing in particular
a prayer to something that answers

effects.desc: the believers stop speaking to anyone who does not believe
the believers build, and what they build has no use
the believers burn what they built before
the believers walk out of the cities
the believers count, and nothing else
the believers kneel, wherever they are, when it comes
the believers refuse the cure and hide the sick
the believers carry it to whoever will listen, on purpose

carriers.desc: it travels in words; a sentence is enough
it travels in images; a glance is enough
it travels as a proof, and is caught by whoever follows it to the end
